title: Vertigo at the Bedside: BPPV Versus Central Causes
subject: ENT
preview: Brief positional vertigo triggered by head movement suggests BPPV, whereas continuous severe vertigo requires broader assessment.
quickRevision: Brief positional vertigo triggered by head movement suggests BPPV, whereas continuous severe vertigo requires broader assessment.
A bedside positional test supports BPPV when performed and interpreted correctly.
HINTS examination has constraints and should be used by trained clinicians in the appropriate acute vestibular syndrome.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Brief positional vertigo triggered by head movement suggests BPPV, whereas continuous severe vertigo requires broader assessment.
Central causes may produce direction-changing nystagmus, marked gait ataxia or focal neurologic deficits.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: A bedside positional test supports BPPV when performed and interpreted correctly.
HINTS examination has constraints and should be used by trained clinicians in the appropriate acute vestibular syndrome.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not assume all dizziness with nausea is benign positional vertigo.

quiz.question: Which feature is more concerning for a central cause of acute vertigo?
options: Severe gait ataxia or focal neurologic deficits
A history of common motion sickness
Brief position-triggered vertigo with characteristic testing
quiz.explanation: Severe gait ataxia or focal neurologic deficits. Central causes may produce direction-changing nystagmus, marked gait ataxia or focal neurologic deficits.
